ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the Canadian Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (DFATD), the Special Economic Measures Act regulations, Canadian domestic PEP databases, and OFAC's SDN list as commercial best practice; heightened due diligence for any non-resident LP partner holding 10% of more; source-of-funds verification, negative news screening, and continuing monitoring throughout the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Centre des entreprises (registre des entreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), the proposed name must be primarily in French, including the legal designation ('Société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'). Names with English-only descriptors are statutorily rejected. Transliteration to Latin script is permitted where original trademarks are involved; all supporting documentation must be attached and French translation certified.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: anything misleading under Criminal Code s. 25 regarding public office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File a written request for extension with the Registraire des entreprises before expiry; if rejected, serve a formal appeal to the registration officer within 30 days of refusal, presenting alternative name options and documentary support. If the refusal is due to similarity with an active name, submit a stamped authorization from the previously registered enterprise or request a review before the Quebec Court of Quebec (civil division) according to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited – a virtual office will be accepted only if a real, verifiable street address within Quebec is provided for service of process; a bare post-office box or mail-forwarding address is rejected. The AI/AV sector does not require physical premises, but the registered office must remain in Quebec.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2242 and 2250 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), arts. 26-55 (declaration and registration); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Legal Publicity of Enterprises system (SLE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration / Application for Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) filed under art. 31 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up or escrow capital is required for a Quebec limited partnership. The general partner(s) must declare their contributions; limited partners must contribute the amounts agreed in the partnership agreement. Non-resident persons may be limited partners and no Canadian residency condition is imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the general partner of the Limited Partnership (the 'LP'), that: (1) the proposed partnership agreement and declaration be approved for registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; (2) the registered office be fixed at the initial business address in Quebec, Province of Quebec, as stated in the declaration; (3) the general partner and each limited partner subscribe to the LP's interests according to the agreed capitalized contributions, which are recorded in the LP register; (4) the named representative be appointed as authorized manager for administrative, regulatory, taxation, and banking matters; and (5) this resolution remain in force until amended by a subsequent written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration name clearance and enterprise declaration preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Online Public Services (Explorateur d'entreprises).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search in the Quebec enterprise database to ensure the proposed limited partnership name is distinctive and complies with the Legal Publicity of Enterprises Regulation.  Prepare the draft declaration containing the LP name, principal establishment address in Quebec, object (AI video synthesis software), names and domiciles of all general partners, contributions and nature, and any other prescribed information.  The declaration may be prepared in French or English, but a French version is recommended for registry acceptance.
required_dossiers: Completed name search / distinctiveness check confirmation
Proposed limited partnership name (Latin characters)
Primary and secondary Quebec activity classification codes (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 mapping where accepted)
Identification of all general partner(s), including corporate registration number if applicable
Identification of limited partner(s) with proposed contribution amounts
Proposed principal establishment address in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, promptly submit an amended declaration with a secondary submitted name, provide supporting evidence of distinctiveness, or convert the declaration to a numbered LP name. Registry corrections do not require re-payment of the registration fee if made within the same application file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the limited partnership agreement and contribution records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel (Quebec lawyer); notary if real property is contributed or if the partners elect notarial form.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The general partner and all limited partners must execute a written partnership agreement setting out: identity of parties, legal nature of the société en commandite, allocation of profits and losses, capital contributions, withdrawal rights, management authority of general partners, and dissolution events.  Although registration can occur before the internal agreement, best practice is to execute the agreement prior to filing the declaration to avoid inconsistencies.  All signatures may be electronic or wet-ink; no notarization is statutorily required for a software services LP unless the agreement conveys immovable rights.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement signed by all general partners and limited partners
Initial capital contribution schedule and subscriptions
Certified copies of government-issued identification for individual partners
Certificate of corporate registration or legal existence for any corporate general partner
Registered office consent (lease, sublease, or notarized authorization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry rejects a term or contribution schedule, amend the agreement by a supplementary written partner resolution; if the registry requires notarized signatures or certified translations, obtain a notarial attestation or professional translation before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Online Submission Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Declaration of Registration using the SLE online system or a paper form to the Registraire des entreprises, pay the statutory fee, and attach the partnership agreement if required by registry practice. The Registrar will process the declaration and issue the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).  The LP is constituted as a legal entity for third-party liability purposes and all statements become public record.  After registration, the general partner must maintain accurate partnership registers.
required_dossiers: Final signed declaration of registration
Executed limited partnership agreement
General partner consent to act
Payment receipt for the filing fee
Power of attorney or authorisation if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire sends a notice of inadmissibility, the filer has the right to correct and resubmit the declaration within 30 days. Correct any missing information, ensure French-language adequacy, or provide compliant governing documents. Late re-filings may incur a small administrative charge but do not dissolve the LP once registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and federal/provincial compliance identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued NEQ and LP resolution, apply for a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA, and register for GST/HST under Excise Tax Act and QST under Quebec Taxation Act.  Obtain separate registrations for payroll source deductions if employees will be engaged.  For the AIGC video SaaS business, apply for an import/export account only if cross-border transfers require it.  Signatory officers must validate their identity with CRA and Revenu Québec.
required_dossiers: NEQ registration confirmation
Pro-forma board/general partner resolution appointing tax representatives
Limited partnership identification documents (contract and declaration)
Canadian bank account proof or anticipated opening arrangement
Names and addresses of general partners and all persons with signing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec delays registration or issues a query, respond through the respective business registration call centres; provide the NEQ, corrected signed authority, and resubmit Form RC159 or Revenu Québec LM-1 as needed. Any penalty for late registration can be remitted under taxpayer relief provisions if caused by registry delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration memorials, annual maintenance, and physical establishment clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises, local municipal permit office, and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registration, establish the physical registered office and ensure the principal establishment is in a commercial zone permitted to conduct software publishing services. File the annual declaration with the Registraire within the prescribed period and maintain the partnership book with records of all partners and contributions. If the LP employs personnel, register with CNESST for occupational health and safety and arrange for group insurance plans as applicable. For the software/AI business, no industrial permit is required, but fire safety and occupancy certificates must be obtained before use of the premises.
required_dossiers: Proof of active registered office address (lease or utility statement)
Municipal occupancy certificate or zoning compliance letter
Fire safety inspection certificate for office occupancy
Annual declaration template and completed information for first fiscal year
Employee payroll and CNESST registration documents (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, file immediately online and pay the prescribed late fee; if the local municipality issues a non-conformity notice for the office, relocate quickly or obtain a variance permit. CNESST registration anomalies are cured by correcting employer classification codes and reported payroll.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies. For reference, the digital economy portfolio is supported by Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE), but ISIC 6201 software and AI video generation do not require an operating licence under Quebec industrial laws.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (ICAI video synthesis and virtual avatar generation is an unregulated software service under Quebec's commerce legislation; no specific operating permit is mandated at the provincial level).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration Exempt — the ordinary business of AI video software creation does not trigger a required EIA under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2). Office-based operations have negligible environmental footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by software operations; comply with municipal stormwater and sanitary sewer discharge bylaws. Any minimal HVAC emissions must meet regional clean air standards under Q-2, s. 20. Electronic waste (servers and monitors) must be handled through approved Recyc-Québec take-back programs; hazardous waste manifest is not required unless non-standard materials are used.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A fire safety certificate for the office occupancy must be obtained from the local fire prevention service under the Fire Safety Act. For any server rooms or raised computer floors, a structural load inspection certificate or written assurance from a Quebec-registered engineer is required to confirm the floor can support the installed equipment. A workplace occupational clearance must be issued by the municipal permit office and, where employees work, a CNESST prevention program must be established.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal income tax and GST/HST administration; Revenu Québec — Quebec income tax and QST administration. Digital portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec Online Services (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident limited partnership carrying on business in Quebec: (1) determine whether GST/HST registration is mandatory by testing the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold on taxable supplies made in Canada; (2) apply to CRA for a general Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 or the My Business Account portal, submitting constituent partnership documents and non-resident status information; (3) activate the GST/HST program account under program account code RM (or the simplified non-resident GST/HST account for pure digital suppliers); (4) register with Revenu Québec for the QST account, obtain the Quebec Establishment Number (NEQ), and link the QST number to the BN; (5) use the BN and QST/NEQ as the sole statutory tax identifiers. No separate VAT ID is issued by Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (income tax transparency under ITA s. 96; for GST/HST and QST purposes, the partnership is treated as a separate 'person' required to register, collect, and remit, while partners remain jointly and severally liable).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists under Canadian federal or Quebec tax law; the limited partnership's pass-through character is statutory. Available partnership-specific elections include: (i) a fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(4) for certain non-calendar-year partnership fiscal periods; (ii) ITA s. 98(3) election on a partnership termination to effect a deemed sale or continuation of Canadian property; (iii) elections under the Excise Tax Act for related registrants to self-assess on supplies between members (s. 156 election), and (iv) Quebec elections under the Taxation Act mirroring federal rules. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA s. 18.4–18.6 are mandatory and no elective opt-out is available; Quebec adopts a provincial hybrid mismatch regime integrated with CRA administration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax, excise-type VAT under the Excise Tax Act) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax, administered by Revenu Québec under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: the small-supplier threshold for GST/HST registration applies to total taxable supplies made in Canada (excluding zero-rated supplies) in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; for non-resident digital-service suppliers of AI video-generation software, the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to Canadian consumer/destination market revenue, triggering mandatory simplified non-resident GST/HST registration. QST registration threshold is aligned with GST/HST at CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, government API pre-clearance, or digital invoice stamping is mandatory under Canadian GST/HST or Quebec QST. Tax invoices need only contain prescribed data (BN/QST registration number, date, nature of supply, tax rate, amount). Electronic invoices are accepted without pre-clearance. Quebec imposes mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST/QST returns and certain data reports for large businesses, but not a transactional clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% GST/HST and 0% QST when the supplier exports them from Canada in accordance with the Excise Tax Act and QST regulations (shipment to an address outside Canada within a commercially reasonable time, with physical export documentation). Services such as AI video-generation SaaS qualify for zero-rating when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside Canada, is not registered for GST/QST, and where the supply does not fall within exclusions such as services rendered to tangible personal property or real estate situated in Canada; the non-resident's Canadian use of the service must be incidental or the supply must meet the place-of-use rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Electronic Export Declaration (e-manifest/EDI export report or legacy Form B13A)
Commercial Invoice and Sales Contract clearly stating the 0-rated supply and service description
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Electronic Cargo Manifest proving shipment from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank FX settlement record showing repatriation to the Canadian partnership bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec audit export zero-rating claims by matching export documents, transportation records, non-resident recipient identity, and FX inflows. Disallowed zero-rating results in retrospective reassessment of net GST/HST and QST, plus statutory interest. Civil penalties apply under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec tax legislation, including 5–50% of net tax for false statements and a 25% gross negligence penalty under the Income Tax Act for knowing misrepresentations; criminal exposure for willful evasion exists under ETA s. 354 and Criminal Code s. 380. The normal four-year reassessment limitation period is removed where fraud or misrepresentation is proven, permitting unlimited retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with exchange-control policy formally resting with the Department of Finance Canada, prudential bank supervision under the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and cross-border funds-flow compliance under the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) pursuant to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in both current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada maintains a free-floating Canadian dollar with no central-bank exchange licensing, no prior approval for remittances, no requirement to route payments through a designated bank, and no restriction on foreign-currency bank accounts. Profit-remittance and capital-flow hurdles are tax-driven only: the Quebec limited partnership must compute and remit Canadian income tax and provincial levy exposures attributable to non-resident partners under Income Tax Act s.135 and Part X III (for interest, royalties, or management-fee-type flows), and treaty resident participants may claim reduced rates only after delivering valid residency certificates (e.g., NR301 form in Quebec or IRS Form 6166 in the United States). Partners whose aggregate specified foreign property exceeds C$100,000 must file Form T1135. No currency convertibility licence or investment-registration condition applies to AIGC software exports or SaaS subscriptions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender ratio, no mandatory conversion timeline, no statutory repatriation period, and no requirement to convert foreign-currency receipts into CAD. The LP may invoice in CAD, USD, EUR, or any convertible currency and may retain export proceeds offshore or in foreign-currency accounts at its Canadian bank. Tax guardrails apply on realization of foreign-exchange gains and losses, and the partnership must maintain an FX translation ledger, support GST/QST input tax credits on foreign-currency acquisitions, and either compute taxable income in CAD under the CRA's functional-currency rules or elect to report in the partnership's functional currency where permitted.

Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — cross-border payments, USD sweep lines, partnership deposit structures
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — treasury API banking, dedicated partnerships unit, integrated FX and commercial card
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — global correspondent network, USD clearing in Latin America and Asia
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — innovation-economy packages, flexible onboarding for cross-border limited partnerships

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — Quebec-domiciled full-service bank, Canadian and French-language corporate KYC, capital markets desk for FX hedging
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account — Quebec cooperative banking group, local commercial account managers, strong digital merchant integration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — legally viable as collection-level rails (Stripe, Paddle, Wise, Payoneer) but not acceptable as the primary treasury or capital-escrow bank. Canada has no separate 'EMI' licence class; non-bank financial technology providers operate as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under the PCMLTFA. An offshore digital EMI providing services to a Canadian LP must be FINTRAC-registered as an MSB, identify beneficial owners of the LP, and report international electronic fund transfers of C$10,000 or more. Quebec does not offer a provincial EMI charter; provincial consumer-protection and data-residency rules (Law 25) apply to platform functionality. Recommended split: use Stripe and Paddle for SaaS collection, allow an MSB for payout concentration, and preserve the Schedule I bank account for capital calls, tax remittances, ISDA-documented hedging, and Lynx/CHIPS clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for physical appearance. All major Canadian banks now permit remote account opening for a Quebec-registered limited partnership using digital identity verification, executed resolutions or partnership declarations, and electronic signatures. A live compliance interview is typically required whenever any general partner or limited partner with 25% or more beneficial ownership is a non-resident individual or a foreign entity; this interview may be conducted by videoconference but is accepted more readily when at least one authorized signatory is physically present in Canada. In practice, full 'touchless' onboarding without any branch visit is available where ownership is wholly Canadian-resident; where non-resident ownership exists, banks commonly request a Montreal or Toronto in-branch appointment to shorten decision time from 6–8 weeks to 2–3 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership — non-resident limited partners or an offshore general partner in a high-risk jurisdiction triggers enhanced due diligence and potential refusal under FINTRAC advisories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec registre des entreprises LP declaration, full limited partnership agreement with capital-call schedule, an ownership chart traced to ultimate natural persons, valid passport copies and tax-residence certificates for each 25%+ owner, apostilled constitutional documents of the general partner, and prior-bank references for every contributing partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible AIGC/SaaS revenue model with no local physical office or payroll — false-positive on automated business-activity filters and Quebec Revenue administrative indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered corporate and partnership identifiers, GST/QST registration confirmations, executed SaaS subscription and licensing agreements, Stripe/Paddle settlement statements, cloud infrastructure invoices from AWS or GCP, a PIPEDA and Quebec Law 25 privacy-program file, and a short economic-substance memorandum from Quebec counsel documenting the LP's actual generation of AI video synthesis services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency-linked capital injections or high-frequency low-value wires resembling structuring or intermingling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A 'fiat-only capital injection' resolution passed by the general partner, bank statements from the funding partners evidencing each wire, an internal capital ledger mapped to LP interests, signed declarations disclaiming crypto-asset conversion immediately preceding each transfer, and bank records evidencing FINTRAC large-EFT and suspicious-transaction-reporting compliance on all C$10,000-plus flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership treasury pooling or service-company mischaracterisation — where the LP appears to be a front for the corporate general partner or a vehicle for partner cash concentration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A separate zero-balance account for the general partner, quarterly management accounts for the LP, filed T5013 and T5013SUM partnership returns, a thin-capitalization analysis under ITA s.18(4) for any partner debt, a written treasury mandate restricting the bank account to AI-business liquidity only, and a monthly reconciliation of the LP capital-account ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all partner capital contributions as SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pacs.009 after bank migration) wires to the LP's tier-1 Canadian bank, settling in CAD on the Lynx system and in USD via CHIPS/Fedwire through the bank's New York correspondent. Each wire must identify the LP by its exact registered legal name in Quebec, the account number, the funding partner as the ordering customer, and a purpose narrative 'LP Capital Contribution — investment in AIGC video synthesis software'. The receiving bank will request the source-of-funds pack: the LP agreement's capital-call clause, the contributing partner's recent account statement evidencing fiat origin, and a declaration by the general partner that no crypto-asset conversion occurred before the transfer. Verification is mandatory for every international electronic funds transfer of C$10,000 or more under FINTRAC rules, so the LP should pre-submit its large-value wire questionnaire and beneficial-ownership documentation. Inbound USD contributions should use a segregated USD sub-account to avoid provisional credit risk; CAD inbound wires achieve same-day value on Lynx.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are selected by payment purpose. (i) Routine cross-border vendor and software payments: SWIFT MT103 with unambiguous narratives such as 'royalties', 'license fees', 'data processing', or 'consulting fees', cleared through the bank's international desk in CAD (Lynx), USD (CHIPS/Fedwire), or EUR (TARGET2). (ii) Domestic Canadian supplier payments: Canadian EFT via the Real-Time Rail or Lynx for high-value same-day credits. (iii) High-value AI hardware and GPU cluster purchases on 30–90 day terms: bank-issued MT700 Commercial Letter of Credit, supplemented by an MT760 standby letter of credit where performance security is required. (iv) AIGC licensing and royalty distributions to rights-holders: MT103 wires after monthly Canadian withholding analysis and GST/QST settlement. (v) Profit distributions to non-resident partners: execute only after computing the partnership's liability under ITA s.135 and Quebec rules, issue T5013/T5013SUM slips, and instruct the wire with purpose 'partnership distribution'. The LP will never co-mingle owner draws with trade disbursements in a single payment instruction and should pre-set same-day FX conversion at the disbursing bank to stabilise net settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNH contracted with the LP's Schedule I bank treasury desk under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and standard Credit Support Annex; tenors up to 24 months with monthly rolling.
Cross-currency basis swaps in CAD versus USD, EUR, or CNH to convert dual-currency SaaS revenue and operating costs into a matched funding currency; benchmarked to CORRA, SOFR, or EURSTR.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies, including INR, BRL, CNY, and MXN, quoted by the bank's offshore NDF desk and settled in CAD at fixing.

Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (risk reversals) for hedging USD-denominated subscription backlog, subject to the LP's non-speculative treasury policy and full hedge-designation records.

Over-the-counter FX swaps used solely for converting daily cash balances without income-statement volatility, executed under the same ISDA Master Agreement and logged in the partnership's treasury hedge register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the month following the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration with the REQ; e.g., registration anniversary on March 15 → filing due by April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a late-fee assessment and, after formal default notice, administrative strike-off of the enterprise; a struck-off limited partnership loses legal publicity and cannot lawfully pursue commercial activities in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal annual filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the fifth month after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, due by May 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of C$25 per partner per month, up to a maximum of C$2,500 per partner; continued failure may result in additional fines, prosecution, and disallowance of partnership losses allocated to partners.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a non-reporting Quebec limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Quebec Limited Partnership Act. Mandatory audit may arise from the partnership agreement, lender/investor requirements, or if the LP becomes a reporting issuer or otherwise becomes subject to securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default framework for a private entity; IFRS may be required if the partnership is publicly accountable, has lender-imposed covenants, or if the partnership agreement mandates IFRS. Tax reporting under the Income Tax Act generally follows the accounting method used consistently and accepted by the CRA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation for limited partnerships. The annual declaration must disclose every general (unlimited) partner and all limited partners and reflect any changes in control or partnership interests. If a partner with significant control changes during the year, that change must be reflected in the next annual declaration and, where applicable, in an updated registration filed with the REQ within the statutory delay. The T5013 return must identify partners receiving income allocations for federal income tax purposes, but this does not constitute a public UBO filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General (Unlimited) Partners and Limited Partners
Register of Contributions and Profit-Sharing Arrangements
Minute Book / Partnership Resolutions and Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–18,000 if an audit is required or voluntarily engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec provincial corporate income tax rate for general active business income (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% and Quebec rate to 3.2% on active business income up to CAD 500,000 (federal) and CAD 500,000 (Quebec) combined business limit, subject to associated corporation aggregation rules and income thresholds; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits up to 35% refundable for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs); Quebec Innovation Tax Credit for AI/software development up to 26% on eligible salaries and certain expenses, non-refundable unless qualifying; Patent box regime under Quebec offers 50% deduction on qualifying innovation income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) GST/HST NETFILE/EFILE, or through CRA My Business Account; Quebec RL-1000 (Revenu Québec file) filed via Revenu Québec's electronic filing system 'EFILE' or 'Retail'
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within six months after the fiscal year-end; Quebec corporate return (RL-1000) due no later than six months after the end of the fiscal year, but if the corporation carries on business or has a permanent establishment in Quebec and the federal T2 deadline applies, use same deadline; balance-due payment due within two months after fiscal year-end (three months for certain CCPCs with low taxable income amounts)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation identification: name, address, business number (BN/NE), incorporation jurisdiction, fiscal year-end date, and language of filing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident limited partnership, do not file T2 as the partnership itself; each non-resident limited partner must file T3 (Partnership Information Return) or T2 if the partner is a corporation, reporting allocable Canadian-source business income; indicate the partnership's CRA program account and list each partner's share

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute net income (accounting income reconciled to tax basis), adding back non-deductible expenses and deducting allowable items, then determine taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source allocable income for non-resident partners; ensure no deduction of foreign expenses not incurred in earning Canadian income; determine taxable income using treaty relief where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 400 / Schedule 400 (Provincial or Territorial Corporation Income Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income to Quebec and other provinces using a permanent establishment formula based on gross revenue and gross salaries/wages in Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the limited partnership has a permanent establishment in Quebec but the corporate partner is non-resident, allocate income using the same formula; non-resident partners without a permanent establishment in Canada may be exempt under an applicable tax treaty

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate Part I tax payable at federal rate and provincial tax payable before credits, then deduct available investment tax credits and federal/provincial tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners are not eligible for the SBD or most refundable credits; claim treaty-related adjustments only through the federal T2 return, and ensure DTA provisions are reflected in the provincial allocation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment of any balance of tax due after crediting instalments, where tax instalments are due quarterly for corporations with tax payable above CAD 3,000
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must make instalment payments if anticipated Canadian federal/provincial tax exceeds CAD 3,000; remit via wire transfer or via a Canadian financial institution using the CRA/Revenu Québec payment reference numbers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For AI/avatar software development, claim eligible SR&ED expenditures (salaries, contracts, materials) and track supporting documentation such as technical problem definitions, hypotheses, experimentation records, and project summaries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations are ineligible for refundable SR&ED credits; only non-refundable credits may be claimed, carried forward 20 years, but for non-residents without taxable Canadian income the credit has no practical benefit; no claim through a pass-through limited partnership unless the corporate partner itself undertakes the SR&ED activity

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under subsection 162(1) and (2) of the Income Tax Act: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty up to 10%; late instalment interest at average prescribed rate plus 4%; Quebec late filing penalty under Taxation Act (Québec): 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus 0.5% per month up to 12 months; failure to file information returns (T3/T5013) penalties up to CAD 100 per day per return (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 7,500); gross negligence penalties up to 50% of any understated tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident corporate partner, reduced to 5% under the Canada-US treaty and 15% under many other DTA treaties if the beneficial owner is a company that holds at least 10% of the voting stock; for limited partnership distributions, the characterization follows the underlying corporate partner status and withholding applies at the corporate level only when the partnership is a specified investment flow-through (SIFT) or when the distribution is from a Canadian-resident corporate payer
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced withholding under a DTA, the non-resident corporate partner must obtain a certificate of residence from its home jurisdiction tax authority and file NR301 (for treaty-based relief) with the payer or provide the appropriate IRS/Canada form under the Canada-US treaty; for Quebec withholding purposes, file Revenu Québec Form RQ-17V; the Canadian partnership must maintain current TRC forms and allocate withholding tax at source on all deemed dividends or partnership income allocations; if the DTA does not apply to Quebec, Quebec may levy an additional 12% withholding on certain dividends paid to non-residents; relief is not automatic and requires validly executed TRC submitted before payment date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% on royalties (including software licensing and IP use), 25% on interest paid to non-residents at large; treaty rates typically: 10% on royalties under most DTAs, 0-10% on interest; Canada-US treaty reduces royalties to 0% for copyright royalties (including software) and 10% for patents and know-how; interest to non-resident arm's-length lenders is exempt from Canadian withholding if paid on an arm's-length basis to a lender not carrying on business in Canada

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 or more in gross revenue per fiscal year and transactions with non-resident non-arm's-length persons exceeding CAD 250,000 (gross) trigger mandatory contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation; transactions below CAD 250,000 are not exempt, they are only excluded from the formal documentation penalty regime
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicability of Economic Substance Regulations (ESR): Canadian federal and Quebec law do not apply the OECD-style ESR with prescriptive substance thresholds applicable in zero-tax jurisdictions; but general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act and Quebec's statutory anti-avoidance rule (SAAR) require genuine business purpose and economic substance; for limited partnerships engaged in AI avatar video generation, the partnership must maintain local substance: physical office (Quebec), Canadian-resident employees, board meetings, management decision-making, and bank accounts; a partnership without substantive Canadian activities may be vulnerable to treaty shopping allegations and denial of DTA benefits under the OECD base erosion and profit shifting (BEPS) framework

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence making false statements or omissions in T2/RL-1000 filings, or maintaining dual sets of books to underreport AI software revenue; deliberately failing to file tax returns; claiming fictitious SR&ED expenditures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under subsection 239(1) of the Income Tax Act, sanction of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded as a civil penalty; criminal prosecution on indictment carries a fine of CAD 10,000 to CAD 200,000 (or 50% of evaded tax if greater) plus imprisonment up to 5 years; Quebec under Tax Administration Act sections 52 and 53: fine of 50% of hidden income and penal prosecution up to CAD 20,000 and imprisonment up to 18 months for tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner of the limited partnership are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes, GST/HST, payroll deductions, and penalties under subsection 227.1 of the Income Tax Act, if they failed to exercise due diligence in ensuring remittances; civil restitution via fraudulent conveyance actions; travel bans under criminal court orders; imprisonment up to 5 years; directors cannot hide behind the corporate veil for tax evasion where they participated in the deception

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in transactions that are an abuse of the tax law, including aggressive loss utilization, circular financing, or artificial allocation of income away from Canada to a zero-tax shell without real business purpose; artificial pricing of AI licensing fees to a non-resident related party to leave Canadian partnership with little profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR disallows the tax benefit and reassesses tax payable plus interest and penalties (up to 25%); Quebec SAAR applies the same denial; no criminal penalty if no fraudulent intent, but additional tax plus interest applies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for resulting tax deficiencies if they signed tax returns knowing the avoidance transaction lacked substance; no imprisonment absent criminal intent, but asset freeze and personal damages under oppression remedies if undue tax advantage diverted partnership funds

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the limited partnership as a bare holding vehicle with no employees, no Quebec office, no active management, and no real AI development, but collecting significant income from AI avatar software sales and streaming royalties; claiming treaty benefits without meeting beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA treaty relief under the limitation-of-benefits clause and general substance-over-form doctrine; reassessment with full 25% withholding tax on all distributions plus interest and late-payment penalties; in Quebec, registration as a shell corporation may be cancelled; no separate tax statute specifically penalizes shell status but penalties for false certification apply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are personally exposed for unpaid withholding taxes under Canadian excise tax and income tax statutes; may face personal criminal liability for money laundering under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act if shell was used to mask beneficial ownership; travel bans and asset seizure possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as a Money Service Business (MSB) when receiving payments via Stripe/Paddle without maintaining AML compliance; failing to verify identity of non-resident corporate partners; processing subscriptions without a compliance program; not reporting suspicious transactions involving AI avatar video software customers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 for each violation for corporations, up to CAD 500,000 for directors; criminal penalties up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for knowingly contravening FINTRAC requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are personally liable for AML penalties if they authorized or acquiesced in the non-compliance; court may impose restitution, freezing of personal assets, and travel restrictions pending criminal investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting transfer prices for intercompany AI software licensing, data feeds, or avatar generation services with related non-resident parties that are not arm's-length and failing to prepare contemporaneous documentation; or failing to disclose such transactions on prescribed Form T106 (and Quebec Form GHG-15) when thresholds are met
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under subsection 247(3) of the Income Tax Act, transfer pricing penalty equal to 10% of the amount of net adjustment on the understated income (or overstated loss) that exceeds the lesser of CAD 5 million and 10% of gross revenue; also interest and possible criminal fines if fraudulent intent; Quebec penalty similar (10% of adjustment)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally assessed for transfer pricing penalties only if they caused the partnership to be reckless in documentation; no direct statutory personal liability for the corporate partner's own tax, but if the partner is a foreign entity, the general partner's directors may be personally liable under Quebec civil code for negligence causing partnership damages

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit on Non-Resident Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not withholding 25% (or treaty reduced rate) on partnership allocations or deemed dividend distributions paid to a non-resident corporate partner, or not filing the required NR4-NR6 forms and Remittance Voucher
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding failure penalty under section 227 of the Income Tax Act: the withholding agent (the partnership or general partner) is liable for the full amount plus interest; penalty 10% of the amount not withheld, up to CAD 10,000; if knowingly fails, penalty of 20% plus imprisonment up to 5 years under tax evasion provisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the general partner are personally liable for all withheld amounts and penalties under due diligence tests; they cannot shield behind the partnership veil because the Act imposes direct joint and several liability on the general partner's directors
